headline: Value-based RL reportedly generalizes robot-policy improvement across simulated tasks
summary: A 4 November arXiv preprint studies online post-training of the pi_0.5 vision-language-action policy across simulated manipulation tasks. The authors report that critic-guided recipes—off-policy generative policy optimization (OGPO) and best-of-N (BoN)—increasingly improve success on held-out scenes and objects as training-task diversity grows, while filtered supervised fine-tuning often forgets on unseen objects. In MolmoSpaces, they report up to +58 percentage points on unseen scenes and +39 points when both scene and object change; one 16-task BoN run used 2.9× fewer gradient steps than 16 single-task runs at matched data-collection budget. These are paper-reported results from three training seeds, not an independent reproduction. The evaluation is simulation-only; on the more challenging LIBERO suite the authors report similar patterns but generalization often gave way to forgetting.
